The engine is opened with template base plus the arm (record_access forced False, storage tempdir: SQLite records, LanceDB vectors, tantivy BM25 index, one store per conversation). Ingest (write path, outside this screen) has already stored one episodic record per turn, embedded it, indexed it in tantivy and tagged speaker perspective (memories.episodic.policies.perspective heuristic).

Query analysis (rules, zero model calls). read() sees no v2 flag, so the plan stage is skipped. _read_planned opens the read scope, date filter (none) and record scope, and looks in the read cache (off). _read fixes mode=replay, budget=_reply_budget (reserve 0, so 4096) and asks for read headers (cards, profile, novelty, slots, digest, recent are all off, so none). Rule classifiers then fire: is_set_question (list_trigger default set_question) turns list mode on for this read, is_ordering (first, latest, before) will sort the final turns by time, resolve_question builds the question perspective (asker, named speakers known to the store) for the perspective leg and the relevance multiplier, query_interval parses an absolute or yearless date span for the temporal leg.

Embed the query and size the candidate window. The query is embedded once with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B after the arm's instruction prefix ('Instruct: Given a question about a user's past conversations, retrieve memories that answer it / Query: ' + question), unit-normalised, 1024 dims. _assemble_core asks _search for want = top_k x pool = 10 x 2 = 20 candidates (pool is max(candidate_pool, list_pool 3) = 3, so 30, when list mode fired). Because hybrid is on, each leg fetches fetch_k = want x LEXICAL_FETCH_MULTIPLIER 3 = 60 (90 in list mode). If the gates later leave fewer than want live candidates, fetch_k is multiplied by 4 and the legs are re-run, up to a 64x widening.

steps.what: Vector leg. LanceDB returns the fetch_k nearest stored turn vectors by cosine distance; the score is 1 - distance. Equal-score runs are settled by content order so the cut is deterministic. This leg is the base of the 'semantic' family.

BM25 leg. The question is tokenised with the content field's analyser (lower-cased alphanumeric runs, no stemming; lexical_analyzer default) and searched in tantivy as a Must namespace term AND an OR of Should content terms. tantivy's BM25 (Okapi, k1 1.2 / b 0.75 defaults) scores them; the leg returns fetch_k hits. A failed lexical leg degrades to vector-only, never an error.

Temporal leg (base template temporal_leg, plus temporal_leg_mentions). Only fires when the question holds a date or a relative phrase resolvable to a span ('12 June 2020', 'in March'; a relative phrase needs temporal_relative, which is off, so those name no span). Records whose valid_from lies in the span, and turns whose own text names a date that overlaps the span (mentioned_spans, resolved against the turn's time), are ranked by closeness to the span's middle; the leg is a NamedLeg('temporal') and is dropped when empty.

Perspective and speaker-vote legs (read.perspective_mode subject_weight, list_mode). perspective leg: records tagged as about the question's subject, in vector order, top list_vote_top_k 30, as NamedLeg('perspective'). speaker_vote leg (only when list mode fired): the vector leg is re-fetched 100 deep (list_vote_depth), kept to the turns of the one speaker the question names (top 30), as NamedLeg('speaker_vote'); two named speakers with a comparison cue vote once each.

Fusion and the protected pool (legacy per-leg path, family_fusion off). rrf_fuse(vector, lexical, extra legs, k=60) adds 1/(60+rank) per leg per record, ties broken by the per-leg rank tuple; scores are divided by the theoretical maximum (legs/(k+1)) so relevance is in [0,1]; the fused list is cut to top_k x widen. Then pool_protect_per_leg=3 re-adds each leg's own top 3 hits that fell below the cut (per_leg mode, so the pool can grow by up to legs x 3).

Gates, perspective multiplier, pool cut. _gate_hits re-reads each id and drops: records missing or not ACTIVATED (archived, superseded, deleted), quarantined, consent-purpose failures, gate4 (off), grant bookkeeping, cues, group/tag filters, passive sessions; cold-tier content is inflated. Then the perspective multiplier reweights relevance by 1 - 0.4 x (1 - match) on the subject axis (about the subject 1.0, the subject speaking of others 0.6, about someone else 0.0) and re-sorts. The pool is cut to candidates[:top_k] plus every protected hit beyond it.

Rerank with jina-reranker-v3.5. Each pool record becomes '[type: episodic | ...]\ncontent' (concat_background); the listwise model scores the whole pool in one forward pass (window 64 documents, scores outside the window would stay 0.0). Raw scores are min-max normalised to [0,1] and replace the retrieval relevance (no blend, no confidence gate, no balanced shortlist, no ordering-question skip). Failure degrades to retrieval order.

steps.what: Score and keep. composite_score(record, relevance) with recency, importance and utility weights all 0.0 is just the reranked relevance; integrity is off; rank_pairs orders by score then valid_from then fingerprint; mmr_lambda is None. Because the read was reranked, candidate_pool > 1 and list mode did not fire, rerank_keep=10 cuts the list to the best 10 (in list mode the whole reranked pool, up to 30, is kept). record_access is False so no RETRIEVE event is written.

Assembly (_assemble_core). _decorate annotates relative phrases against each record's own event time ('last <weekday> [= <date>]', resolve_relative_dates + relative_dates_anchored) and wraps instruction-flagged or low-trust records. AssemblyPolicy.assemble then: abstains when the best score < theta 0.25 (never after min-max, the best is 1.0); skips the H4 relative floor (0.3 x best) because the read was reranked and rerank_floor=skip; selects greedily by MMR (lambda 0.7, word-Jaccard redundancy) under the 4096-token budget counted as len//4+1, never returning empty; places stable (non-episodic) records before volatile ones.

Replay windows. In replay mode each selected episodic hit (and the best source turn of any mined fact) is expanded inside its session (episodic.sessions, gap 30 minutes): the hit first, then neighbours nearest-first (older on a tie), 2 turns before and 4 after (replay_window_before/after). A neighbour that is hidden by the gates, already present, or does not fit the remaining 4096 tokens (len//4+1) is skipped; it never costs the hit its place. In list mode hits ranked beyond window_full_hits=10 are single turns. Turns are sorted chronologically (chrono_key); ordering questions stay in time order; stable records stay first. _render is plain (render != dated).

Hand-off to the reader. The headers/overlays/gates stage is a no-op (relevance_gate off, owner/entity checks off, external off). MemspineSystem.query turns each record into '[YYYY-MM-DD] content' (dated rendering, event date of the record, engine order = stable first then chronological), records span offsets and hit ranks, and the runner truncates by hit rank to 4096 reader tokens if needed (whole lowest-ranked lines go first). The prompt GROUNDED_QA_PROMPT is formatted with {context} and {question}: lines carry [YYYY-MM-DD] said-dates and 'phrase [= date]' resolved dates; give a short direct best-supported answer; say not mentioned only if nothing bears on it; dates in the wording the memories use. One chat completion to qwen3.5:9b via Ollama (temperature 0, max 512 tokens, thinking off, sampler explicit). RefusalRetryReader re-asks once with a neutral firmer instruction when the answer is a refusal on a non-empty context.

Judge. GuardedJudge wraps the rubric-guarded LLM judge: an empty answer is WRONG without a call (--judge-guards); a deterministic date check credits an answer whose first date is the single day the gold names (--judge-date-check); otherwise one qwen3.5:9b call with the rubric prompt (CORRECT only if the same fact as gold, hedging and extra detail allowed, equivalent relative dates credited, do-not-know is WRONG) returns JSON {label}. The score is accuracy over LoCoMo categories 1-4 (1,540 questions); reference result clean-jina-full 81.4% (1,253), mean context 2,097 tokens, p50 764 ms.

Mentions. For each seed the associative store's live 'mentions' edges give the records that mention the entity; records not live (quarantined, archived, other type) are skipped. The role of the entity in each record is subject (record.entity), object (a dst: tag) or mention.

Library scoring. entity_leg_explained scores records per matched entity with the Mem0-style boost, max over matched entities and capped (cap 0.5), with hub damping by entity degree (DampingConfig) so a very common entity does not flood the leg; returns provenance for the wiretap (read.leg.entity).

REF-WRITE.trigger: per write_messages call (a batch of turns); the per-turn loop runs once per depositable turn

steps.what: Entry: Engine.write_messages delegates to ingest.write.write_messages. With write.intake_v2 on it first goes through the intake gateway (envelope, write ids, receipt) which then calls write_messages_direct on the fresh turns; with it off write_messages_direct runs straight away.

Depositable filter: for every turn, skip malformed turns, roles in firewall.skip_message_roles (system/tool by default) and recalled-memory echoes (firewall.skip_injected_recall), and screen the text with the firewall secret redactor, so the list of contents is exactly what will reach the door.

Prewarm embeddings: if at least two distinct depositable contents exist, embed them in chunks of embedding.batch_size so the embedding cache holds every vector before the per-record work (G9). If this embedding fails the call raises before any turn is written, so a retry cannot duplicate turns.

Neighbour prefetch (#63): when the firewall is enabled, the vector store has query_many and there are two or more distinct contents, run the firewall's nearest-neighbour query for all turns as one batched vector search and keep it in a context var for the call.

Open a projection batch (_projection_batch): projectors may defer commits (the lexical index holds its Tantivy commit) and the per-projector high-water marks are checkpointed once at the end instead of once per event.

Per-turn loop _write_turns: role policy decision and the optional stamp (only when their v2 flags are on), per-turn tags (spk/addr perspective, assistant_claim, recommendation, forget-request, correction, idem, asset refs, reference edges), event-time resolution (timestamp or valid_from, session sequence). Each turn then calls Engine.write with memory_type=episodic.

Engine.write builds the MemoryRecord (episodic, SourceInfo role/channel/session, tags, valid_from, pending stamp/role applied), computes the parent trust cap (integrity MTI-D), then takes the per-namespace write lock (eng._write_locks[ns]) and calls _write_locked_ex. This is the write_locked step: one writer per namespace so the firewall's context reads, the write and corroboration are one unit.

Firewall gate 1 (_screen_write): field redaction, governance tags, then the deterministic trust/anomaly/instruction assessment (embedding outlier from the prefetched neighbours, MINJA prefixes, instruction signals, size and protected-key checks), consent store check, W2-04 gate-3 hold, verdict applied to the record (trust set, quarantine flag), hearsay cap, parent trust cap, principal reputation, inferred cap.

Quarantine branch: a held record is appended as a WRITE event with the firewall reasons and stored inert (no dedup, no ladder, no retrieval surface), then returns. Admitted records go to _write_screened.

Event append: a WRITE MemoryEvent with payload.record is appended to the event log through _append_and_project, which assigns the seq (the event log is the truth; every store below is a projection of it).

Projectors apply the event in order, inline: RecordProjector (upsert_record into the records table), VectorProjector (embed record.content through the cache, upsert the vector for the embedder id), LexicalProjector (index the record in tantivy/FTS, commit deferred to the batch flush), GraphProjector (upsert a node labelled with the memory type, plus entity mention nodes/edges when associative.entity_nodes is on). Offsets are held back until the batch flush.

After the append: corroboration and link evolution run (_corroborate, _evolve_links); back in Engine.write the session is reopened if horizon sessions are on, the reply_to link is written, and (if write.window_extract is on and the action was added) the turn is handed to WindowPipeline.observe, which never fails the write.
Leave the projection batch: each projector is flushed (lexical commit), then its high-water mark is written (set_offset). The records of the call are returned.

steps.what: Raw turns land through the reference write path (REF-WRITE). After the episodic WRITE is stored, Engine.write calls WindowPipeline.observe(record, session) for every added episodic turn (quarantined or instruction-flagged turns never enter a window).

Embed the turn (used only for the topic boundary) and feed it to the per-namespace WindowSegmenter. A window closes at the first of: topic shift (cosine of consecutive turns below running mean - k*sd, k=2.0, needs WINDOW_TOPIC_MIN_PAIRS pairs and WINDOW_TOPIC_MIN_TURNS turns), 6 turns, 1500 tokens (4 chars per token), session change, idle (120 s, async only) or flush.

Closed windows are queued as jobs in the in-memory deque (workers.outbox is off). With write.window_async=false (eval arms) nothing runs until Engine.flush_windows(), close_session() or sleep(); then _drain pops each job and runs _run_job under an ops stage 'window_extract'.

_prepare_job: re-read the window's turns from the store and keep only live ones (ACTIVATED, not quarantined, not instruction-flagged); an empty window is skipped. Build the numbered transcript '[n] [YYYY-MM-DD] Speaker: text', the participant list and the turn count.

ONE structured LLM call per window (sections = facts only for window_extract=facts). The call is cached by (model|prompt version|sections|transcript|participants) so a re-run on the same history is free. Prompt window_extract.yaml (JSON, token_budget 4096, temperature 0) is rendered with the sections variable and parsed into WindowPayload by structured_call (llm.structured.retry_on_error adds at most one re-prompt on a validation error).

Validate the facts section item by item (validate_facts): fact_guard shape check, WindowFact model, cited line numbers must exist, and the verbatim span must be a substring of a cited line (grounded()); items failing are counted invalid / uncited / ungrounded and dropped. A malformed section fails closed (dropped, counted), never discarding the other sections.

Deposit each accepted fact through the mined-fact door (_store_facts): text '<entity> <attribute>: <value>', parents = the cited turn records, tags window_fact, window:<id>, spk:<x> (when one speaker), role-basis tag when role policy is on; event date from fact.date (range-checked _fact_date) else window start; kind state keeps the (entity, attribute) key, kind event drops the attribute so the ladder ADDs it. Persons, location and topic become person:/loc:/topic: view tags.

The mined-fact door (record source role 'assistant', channel 'mining') takes the namespace lock, re-checks that all parents and window members are still live (I72), caps trust at the least-trusted parent, then goes through write_derived -> _write_locked -> firewall gate -> semantic pipeline (dedup, entity extraction, conflict ladder) -> event append -> the four projectors. A vanished parent cancels the rest of the window.

S43.trigger: per window of up to 6 turns, drained at flush_windows/close_session/sleep (async off). Reference arm for S44 and S45; reference gc3 = S02 plus this flag

steps.what: Raw turns land through the reference write path (REF-WRITE). After the episodic WRITE is stored, Engine.write calls WindowPipeline.observe(record, session) for every added episodic turn (quarantined or instruction-flagged turns never enter a window).

Embed the turn (used only for the topic boundary) and feed it to the per-namespace WindowSegmenter. A window closes at the first of: topic shift (cosine of consecutive turns below running mean - k*sd, k=2.0, needs WINDOW_TOPIC_MIN_PAIRS pairs and WINDOW_TOPIC_MIN_TURNS turns), 6 turns, 1500 tokens (4 chars per token), session change, idle (120 s, async only) or flush.

Closed windows are queued as jobs in the in-memory deque (workers.outbox is off). With write.window_async=false (eval arms) nothing runs until Engine.flush_windows(), close_session() or sleep(); then _drain pops each job and runs _run_job under an ops stage 'window_extract'.

_prepare_job: re-read the window's turns from the store and keep only live ones (ACTIVATED, not quarantined, not instruction-flagged); an empty window is skipped. Build the numbered transcript '[n] [YYYY-MM-DD] Speaker: text', the participant list and the turn count.

ONE structured LLM call per window (sections = facts only for window_extract=facts). The call is cached by (model|prompt version|sections|transcript|participants) so a re-run on the same history is free. Prompt window_extract.yaml (JSON, token_budget 4096, temperature 0) is rendered with the sections variable and parsed into WindowPayload by structured_call (llm.structured.retry_on_error adds at most one re-prompt on a validation error).

Validate the facts section item by item (validate_facts): fact_guard shape check, WindowFact model, cited line numbers must exist, and the verbatim span must be a substring of a cited line (grounded()); items failing are counted invalid / uncited / ungrounded and dropped. A malformed section fails closed (dropped, counted), never discarding the other sections.

Deposit each accepted fact through the mined-fact door (_store_facts): text '<entity> <attribute>: <value>', parents = the cited turn records, tags window_fact, window:<id>, spk:<x> (when one speaker), role-basis tag when role policy is on; event date from fact.date (range-checked _fact_date) else window start; kind state keeps the (entity, attribute) key, kind event drops the attribute so the ladder ADDs it. Persons, location and topic become person:/loc:/topic: view tags.

The mined-fact door (record source role 'assistant', channel 'mining') takes the namespace lock, re-checks that all parents and window members are still live (I72), caps trust at the least-trusted parent, then goes through write_derived -> _write_locked -> firewall gate -> semantic pipeline (dedup, entity extraction, conflict ladder) -> event append -> the four projectors. A vanished parent cancels the rest of the window.

Because this arm sits on gc3 (graph sleep), the mined window facts then feed the later sleep stages (extract_graph, entity summaries, communities) that run in sleep(); those stages are not part of this flag.

S44.trigger: per window, inside the same extraction job as S43 (replaces the v1 validate/deposit of the facts section)

steps.what: Config check: envelope_v2 requires window_extract with a facts section (config/requires.py). _build_windows builds EnvelopeWrite: EnvelopeCompiler (prompt hash structured@1, kind registry capped at 64), ItemValidator, RepairAsk on the router-bound window_extract LLM (max_tokens 4096), a sqlite FailureLedger (dead-letter list, <path>.deadletters.sqlite), and the stage list (empty here).
Raw turns and window cutting are as S43 (REF-WRITE, WindowSegmenter, queue, _live_turns, numbered transcript).

ONE call per window with the in-code 'structured' prompt (STRUCTURED_SYSTEM, constant system part; user part holds participants and numbered lines). The model must return a JSON ARRAY of ItemV1 objects in compact keys (s, r, o, text, kind, mode, neg, when, until, lines, span, source, speaker, reported_speaker, chg). A reply that is not a JSON list raises LLMError and the window's facts section is dropped.

Validate each item alone (ItemValidator.validate -> compile_items): item parses as ItemV1, at least one cited line exists in the window and is a NEW (non-context) line, no reserved system field (ids, trust, scope, status), non-empty text, kind accepted by the registry. Valid items compile into AssertionEnvelopes with evidence spans, modality (asserted/planned/hoped/asked/hedged plus negation), write id and occurrence id; duplicates are dropped, not repaired.

Repair once: the invalid repairable items go back in ONE repair call (the original messages, only the invalid items as the assistant turn, typed error codes and field paths, no new items allowed). The corrected items are validated again; fixed ones are added, the rest are dead-lettered.

Dead letters: every item still invalid (or a repair call that failed) is recorded in the FailureLedger with window id, index, code, attempts and the item; a failed whole-window call is also recorded with kind=window and retry_allowed.

Deposit each envelope through the mined-fact door (_store_envelopes): text = envelope text, entity = subject surface, tags window_fact, window:<id>, envelope_v2, src:<class>, spk:<x>; parents = the evidence source turns; trust capped by the envelope's source_trust; happened label from the compiled time text; the envelope JSON is kept in the record's fingerprint.envelope. Counters items_valid/repaired/dead are updated.

steps.what: ingest.write.write_messages sees intake_v2 and hands the call to gateway.write_messages: each turn becomes a Segment (seg_index, role, speaker, source_at, content) and the call becomes one SourceEnvelope (kind conversation, source id '<session>#<batch digest>', scope from namespace/session/actor).

IntakeGateway.submit under a per-scope lock: validate_envelope, derive write ids per segment (S3-3: idempotency key = caller id, else a hash of scope, source id, seg_index, content), load the overlay of known writes, and IntakeBook.accept decides new / retry / new_version per segment, checks quota (QuotaExceededError before accept) and builds the receipt.
Retry or no-op: an identical call returns the original receipt and record ids and writes nothing (pending applies are finished in-line first).

Ledger commit: one SQL transaction stores the intent, the receipt, per-write rows and the apply payload (the fresh turns). This is the first crash boundary; before it nothing is stored, so a retry writes everything.

Apply: _apply_messages calls the old door write_messages_direct on the fresh turns only, each tagged idem:<write id>; the record id each write id became is collected through INTAKE_LANDED. On resume it first scans existing records by idem tag so only the missing turns are written. All of REF-WRITE (filter, prewarm, firewall, event, projectors) runs here unchanged.

Mark applied: real record ids and honest readiness (raw_search ready; facts/graph/summaries pending only if a window pipeline exists; profile unavailable) are stored with the receipt; the apply payload is dropped. Recovery at engine start (recover) finishes any intent accepted but not applied.

two-phase commit-then-apply with crash boundaries and idem tags for resume

Build evidence bundles: record_envelope turns the fact plus its turns into an envelope; build_bundles (LIB-06) makes one bundle per fact; shared turns are counted once.

Fill the rest with the other records whole, in rank order; a turn already cited by an included bundle is not repeated (dropped as cited_by_bundle). libraries: LIB-06 exact budget and evidence bundles (src/memspine/compose/budget.py, bundles.py)

steps.what: INTAKE (write.intake_v2). write_messages becomes a SourceEnvelope; IntakeBook assigns write ids and verdicts (new/retry/new_version), checks quota, commits the intent and apply payload in one SQL transaction, then applies the fresh turns through write_messages_direct (tagged idem:<id>) and marks the receipt applied. Crash recovery runs at start.

STAMPING (write.stamping_v2). ConversationStamper stamps each raw turn with three clocks (source_at, source_tz, recorded_at), typed speaker/addressee/participants, provenance class and an assent tag, before the firewall. Downstream, the temporal stage treats source_at as the only source clock (valid_from is no longer read as a source time).

ROLE POLICY (write.role_policy_v2). role_wiring.decide tags every raw turn (derive_use, echo, echo_of, assent_candidate), lowers trust to the role ceiling, and stores system/tool turns raw instead of skipping them. At derivation time _live_turns drops echoes and excluded turns, and facts whose cited turns include no user-stated line get a derive_use:evidence/proposal tag.

SEGMENTATION AND BATCHING (write.segmentation_v2). Each stored episodic turn is fed to a StreamSegmenter (cuts: session change, time gap 1800 s, topic shift, 1500 tokens, adaptive turn cap 6 growing to 24 while under 400 tokens). Closed windows queue; CallBatcher groups windows of one namespace into batches of at most 8 windows / 3000 tokens / 30 s age (final drains release everything). A prepass verdict (none here) could skip a window.

PROMPT V2 (write.prompt_v2), ONE call per window or batch. PromptContextBuilder adds CONTEXT (tail of the previous window, up to 3 lines) and KNOWN (up to 40 entities already in memory from the entity records and alias table, plus resolver and pre-pass hooks). window_messages builds a constant system text (no examples; sections spec for facts; coarse_date and no_injection partials) and a user part (same_language partial for non-English input, participants, NEW, CONTEXT, KNOWN). The call asks for a JSON object {facts:[ItemV1...]}; json_schema constrained decoding is sent when the provider supports it (prompt_schema auto), and is dropped for the run if the backend rejects it. The reply is cached by (model, prompt id, sections, transcript, context, known).

ENVELOPE VALIDATE, REPAIR, DEAD LETTERS (write.envelope_v2). If the whole reply is not a usable JSON object, one reparse re-ask echoes the reply back (reparse_calls). Then _compile_items runs process_items: each ItemV1 is validated alone and compiled to an AssertionEnvelope (citations, NEW-line rule, reserved fields, kind cap 64), invalid repairable items go back in ONE repair call (structured.repair prompt), items still invalid are written to the sqlite FailureLedger (dead letters, with reason code and attempts), duplicates are dropped.
STAGE HOOK LIST runs in order over the window's envelopes, outside the namespace lock (run_envelope_stages sorts by order). Step 8 to 13 are its members.

TEMPORAL, order 100 (write.temporal_v2). For every envelope fill the event interval, precision and basis by the anchor ladder: explicit date in when/until, span or text (EN/DE/FR/ES; year-only stays year precision), else relative phrase resolved against the cited turn's stamped source_at, else (stamping off only) the window valid_from as inferred/approximate, else unknown (never 'now'); typed relations (before/after/during) between assertions of the window when no date resolves. Writes time.event, assessment.time_precision and extras.temporal. No model call.

GROUNDING, order 200 (write.grounding_v2). LIB-03 check_grounding locates the supporting span in the cited lines and writes offsets; rule checks (cited turns exist, numbers/units/dates/names in the span, polarity and modality, speaker matches asserter); undecided items go to the adjudicator, here the lexical-overlap fallback (ground_adjudicator=lexical, no LLM); assent check promotes assistant_proposed to user_confirmed only on a real binding yes. Unsupported/partly are dropped (ground_action=drop), counted by reason code; undecided are kept as grounding=uncertain.

COVERAGE, order 250 (write.coverage_v2). LIB-17 computes coverage = informative lines cited by a kept assertion / informative lines (salience: named entity, number, date, first-person state/plan/preference, list shape; greetings and echoes excluded). If coverage < 0.8 and a line is uncited, ONE targeted re-extraction call covers only the uncited lines (up to 6 targets, 2 context lines) with the window prompt on the window_extract LLM; its items go through the compiler and the earlier stages again (temporal, grounding) and are added only if grounded; everything else is dropped and counted. Cost is booked under stage coverage_reextract.

RESOLVER, order 300 (write.resolver_v2). For the subject and object mention of each envelope: rule resolver (exact, alias, spelling, nickname, numeric, exonym; context conflicts keep homonyms apart), then embedding cosine against the scope's entities (>=0.9 same, 0.7 to 0.9 grey zone, below new) with a bounded vector cache. Result existing / pending_merge / new; sets subject.entity_id / object.entity_id and extras.resolve; MERGE/SPLIT are logged as marker events; never merges on its own. The resolver's entities also feed KNOWN of later prompts.

INTEGRATION, order 400 (write.integration_v2). For each state envelope find live assertions on the same (subject, attribute) key in the semantic store and decide an operator with the ladder: cardinality (declared, else many), trust tier, event time (closed or open interval), negation binding, seeded by change_hint and extras transition/replaces; ops append/supersede/merge/coexist/contest/defer_kc. With no hint that a value changed (integration_decide_unhinted false) a conflicting live value is deferred to K_C instead of decided. The verdict is written on the envelope and becomes record tags (integ:<op>, disputed, retract) at deposit; a contest also tags the older peer disputed.

PRE-PASS, order 500 (write.prepass). OFF in this arm (default 'off'), so neither the window skip, the KNOWN hints nor the cross-check stage is built. When on (rules or GLiNER2 on CPU), it would skip windows with nothing extractable and flag envelopes naming an entity the pre-pass never saw.

DEPOSIT. _store_envelopes deposits each surviving envelope through the mined-fact door (same lock, I72 liveness re-check, trust cap = min(parents, envelope source_trust), firewall gate 2/3, semantic ladder, event append, four projectors): tags window_fact, window:<id>, envelope_v2, src:<class>, integ:*; kind state keeps the (entity, attribute) key, event drops it; happened label from the temporal stage; envelope JSON in fingerprint.envelope. Contest peers are marked disputed. Counters and per-stage notes land in the window stats.

steps.what: Existing extract_graph facts are indexed first: every live or closed fact of the namespace goes into an EdgeKeyIndex by v2 key, by base (from its edge_base: tag) or as a v1 alias key.

For each extracted edge compute the v1 key (namespace, src, rel, dst; with isolation.scope_keys_v2 the tenant+owner identity) and the v2 base key = hash(scope, kind, src, rel, dst, extras) where extras are the event day and numerals for dated event edges.
Occurrence = hash of the sorted cited turns (content fingerprint @ valid_from), so re-extracting the same turns gives the same key (replay idempotent) while a new statement later gives a new one.

EdgeKeyIndex.decide: duplicate if the exact v2 key exists; duplicate via base if a live sibling of the same base exists; duplicate via alias if a live v1 key exists; new_occurrence if only closed siblings exist (the A -> B -> A return); else new.
A 'duplicate' only adds edge_source provenance to the existing fact (no write). A stale duplicate (record closed since) is re-checked against storage and turned into new_occurrence.
A new key is written as the fact's message_id and the base is stored as an edge_base: tag so later occurrences find their siblings. A derive.graph.key tap event records outcome, via and kind.

SLEEP_CYCLE_ORDER = consolidate, mine_facts, anticipate, reflect_profile, extract_graph, summarize_entities, reorganize, check_watches, session_lifecycle, decay_sweep, compress, sleep_compute, event_log_prune. sleep_stage_order() only inserts extra stages when their flag is on (predict_calibrate, project_facts, rule_edges, pattern_observations, standing_answers, reconcile, histories, compile_edges, erasure_rederive, retention_expire); none is on in gc3, so all 13 names run in this order, each timed and costed through run_sleep_stage.

1 consolidate (RUNS, no LLM): detect sessions by a 30-minute gap over live episodic records; for each closed session of at least 3 records write ONE semantic summary record (channel consolidation, parents = the session turns, trust = min of members). No summarize role is bound in gc3, so the text is the deterministic extractive fallback (max 600 chars). It also emits the CONSOLIDATE/session index that extract_graph reads.

2 mine_facts (SKIPPED): consolidation.mine_facts is off and no extract role is bound. 3 anticipate (SKIPPED): consolidation.anticipate off. 4 reflect_profile (SKIPPED): consolidation.reflect_profile off and no reflect role (this is the stage S01/gc9 turns on).

5 extract_graph (RUNS, LLM role extract_edges): granularity=session. Group the live episodic turns of each consolidated session (skipping cues, entity-summary and window-episode records, quarantined or instruction-flagged turns); skip a session whose membership fingerprint already has a stage_done marker. For each remaining session, render a numbered transcript '[n] [date] turn', optionally ask the GLiNER2 decision provider for allowed entity names (only if configured; not in gc3), then ONE structured call (prompt extract_edges@session, 1 round) returns edges {src_entity, rel, dst_entity, fact, kind state|event, valid_from/valid_to, confidence, episode_indices}. Turns not in any consolidated session (sessions under 3 records) fall back to one per-record call with the plain extract_edges prompt.

5b Entity resolution (resolve=rules, no LLM): every src/dst name goes through the ladder exact canonical match -> alias table (MARKER events) -> top-15 embedding candidates (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B) -> entropy gate -> MinHash character-shingle Jaccard >= 0.9, with a trust guard; merges are logged as one entity_resolved MARKER.

5c Write: each edge becomes a semantic fact (content = edge.fact, entity = src, attribute = rel for kind:state, no attribute for kind:event; tags kind:/rel:/dst:; channel extract_graph; parents = the cited turns), written through the semantic door (firewall trust cap, M5 dedup, M4 ladder so a newer state value supersedes). A verbatim duplicate only adds edge_source provenance. Then an asserted LINK from every parent turn to the fact (weight = min of confidence and trusts, subject to the link budget) and a graph_extracted MARKER watermark per source and a per-session stage_done marker.

6 summarize_entities (RUNS, LLM role summarize_entity, only when needed): the graph projector has turned entity/dst names of live records into ent:<ns>:<name> nodes with mentions links (associative.entity_nodes). For each entity node whose member fingerprint changed, build dated fact lines; if the joined lines fit 2000 chars the summary is those lines (free, no call); otherwise entities are batched (30 per call) into prompt summarize_entity.yaml, with a newest-lines fallback on failure. Each result is a derived semantic record (channel entity_summary, tag about:<Name>, parents = the members, trust = min), firewall-screened, and an entity_summarized MARKER stores the watermark.

7 reorganize (SKIPPED in practice): needs a graph store and either the [community] extra (graspologic-native, absent from the dev venv) or community.algorithm=lpa; with the default algorithm auto and no extra it returns skipped. If it did run it would write community summary parents.

8 check_watches, 9 session_lifecycle, 10 decay_sweep, 11 compress, 12 sleep_compute, 13 event_log_prune: check_watches only logs fired prospective watches (none); session_lifecycle needs sessions.passive_after (unset: skipped); decay_sweep moves idle records between tiers by days since recorded_at/last access (all records are fresh in an eval, so no moves); compress zstd-compresses cold-tier content (none cold); sleep_compute is the no-op E7 hook; event_log_prune runs only in rolling event-log mode (skipped).

REF-SLEEP.storage: Reads the event log and the episodic/semantic stores. Appends WRITE events (consolidation summaries, extract_graph facts, entity_summary records), LINK events (asserted, mentions, derived_from), MARKER events (graph_extracted, entity_resolved, entity_summarized, stage_done per session) and DECAY_TRANSITION events (supersede/archive). Projectors update the vector, FTS and graph stores.
REF-SLEEP.cost: Dominated by extract_edges: one 9B call per session at roughly 1.5-2 h for the 10-conversation set (GAP_REGISTER L estimate); the stage list adds no GPU model other than the embedder. Doc: gc3 about 39 min per 3-conversation sample run ('11 gc9 / 24 gc2 / 39 gc3' min engine-LLM ingest in SCREENS.md).
REF-SLEEP.inputs: Episodic turns written with group/session ids and event dates; an extract_edges role; associative memory enabled so the graph projector exists.
REF-SLEEP.outputs: Semantic summaries, graph facts with parents, asserted/mentions links, entity-summary records. The read side then uses read.graph_leg (BFS depth 2, 10 seeds), graph_node_search and read.entity_summaries over these.
failure_modes: A failed extract_edges call leaves no watermark: the session is retried next sweep (errors counted in the stage stats, status partial).
reorganize is a silent skip without graspologic-native: no community summaries in any gc3-based arm unless offline.communities_v2 is on.
Session grouping depends on consolidate having produced a session index; sessions under 3 records are extracted per record.
Sleep has no budget cap in this arm (offline.budget_v2 off): a slow Ollama server stalls the build.
